title: Brian Kernighan and the Origin of 'Hello, World!' (1972-1978)
explainer: The three words you type into five different files didn't start as a teaching convention invented for this course: Brian Kernighan used a 'hello, world' string in a 1972 internal tutorial on the B programming language, and it reached the audience that made it universal six years later in Kernighan and Ritchie's book 'The C Programming Language.' The C version you write in this lesson is essentially the same program that set the template every language tutorial since has copied.

title: Guido van Rossum, Monty Python, and the Naming of Python (1989)
explainer: Guido van Rossum started implementing Python at CWI in the Netherlands in December 1989 and named it after the BBC comedy show Monty Python's Flying Circus, not the snake - he wanted something short and slightly irreverent, and said explicitly it wasn't meant as a joke about reptiles. It's a reminder that a language's name is an artifact of its creator's taste, not a clue to how it works, which is worth noticing now that you're juggling five languages whose names (Python, Java, Bash) all have unrelated, specific origin stories.
